front: Where do the knowledge areas come from?
back: The PMBOK Guide, Sixth Edition. Process Groups: A Practice Guide lists the processes by process group only.

Develop Project Charter; Develop Project Management Plan; Direct and Manage Project Work; Manage Project Knowledge; Monitor and Control Project Work; Perform Integrated Change Control; Close Project or Phase.
Plan Scope Management; Collect Requirements; Define Scope; Create WBS; Validate Scope; Control Scope.
Plan Schedule Management; Define Activities; Sequence Activities; Estimate Activity Durations; Develop Schedule; Control Schedule.
Plan Cost Management; Estimate Costs; Determine Budget; Control Costs.
Plan Quality Management; Manage Quality; Control Quality.
Plan Resource Management; Estimate Activity Resources; Acquire Resources; Develop Team; Manage Team; Control Resources.
Plan Communications Management; Manage Communications; Monitor Communications.
Plan Risk Management; Identify Risks; Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis; Perform Quantitative Risk Analysis; Plan Risk Responses; Implement Risk Responses; Monitor Risks.
Plan Procurement Management; Conduct Procurements; Control Procurements.
Identify Stakeholders; Plan Stakeholder Engagement; Manage Stakeholder Engagement; Monitor Stakeholder Engagement.

front: Which knowledge area has a process in every process group?
back: Integration.

front: Which knowledge areas have no Executing process?
back: Scope, Schedule and Cost.

front: Where is a change request decided?
back: Perform Integrated Change Control (Monitoring and Controlling).
Control Quality: the team checks the deliverable is correct. Validate Scope: the customer formally accepts it.
Manage Quality: the process, in Executing. Control Quality: the product, in Monitoring and Controlling.
Issued by the sponsor. Formally authorizes the project and gives the project manager authority to use resources.
Describes how the project will be executed, monitored and controlled, and closed.

front: The 18 components of the project management plan
back: 10 subsidiary management plans, the change and configuration management plans, 4 baselines, the life cycle description and the development approach.
Scope, schedule, cost, and the performance measurement baseline.

front: Plan component or project document: risk register, issue log, stakeholder register?
back: Project documents. They are not part of the project management plan.
Data: raw measurements. Information: data analyzed in context. Reports: information compiled to prompt decisions or awareness.
